an3.82:1.1: “Monks, it is just as if a donkey were following right after a herd of cattle, saying,
an3.82:1.2: ‘I too am a cow! I too am a cow!’
an3.82:1.3: Its color is not that of a cow, its voice is not that of a cow, its hoof is not that of a cow,
an3.82:1.4: and yet it still keeps following right after the herd of cattle, saying,
an3.82:1.5: ‘I too am a cow! I too am a cow!’
an3.82:2.1: In the same way, there is the case where a certain monk follows right after the Saṅgha of monks, saying,
an3.82:2.2: ‘I too am a monk! I too am a monk!’
an3.82:2.3: He doesn’t have the other monks’ desire for undertaking the training in heightened virtue, doesn’t have their desire for undertaking the training in heightened mind [concentration], doesn’t have their desire for undertaking the training in heightened discernment,
an3.82:2.4: and yet he still keeps following right after the Saṅgha of monks, saying,
an3.82:2.5: ‘I too am a monk! I too am a monk!’
an3.82:3.2: ‘Strong will be our desire for undertaking the training in heightened virtue; strong will be our desire for undertaking the training in heightened mind; strong will be our desire for undertaking the training in heightened discernment.’
an3.82:3.3: That is how you should train yourselves.”
